local_state_rules: A signal can be represented as a sum of sinusoidal components.
Low-pass filtering attenuates components above cutoff; high-pass attenuates below cutoff.
Time-domain waveform, frequency bars, filter mask, and reconstructed signal must stay linked.
difficulty_profile: linked time/frequency views must respond to the same component model
filter controls must change reconstructed signal not only labels
primary visual must be domain-native simulated object, not a pure chart/table/line diagram
task_world.visual_object_requirement: The UI must include a signal-lab simulation with signal generator, filter module, oscilloscope-style time trace, spectrum analyzer bars, and connected signal path; a waveform/curve alone is not sufficient.

validation_scenarios.name: Fourier explanation and linked views
validation_scenarios.public_requirement_ref: T1 asks for explanation and interactive Fourier signal UI.
validation_scenarios.oracle: Assistant text explains decomposition; UI shows component controls plus time waveform and frequency bars that update together. The primary visual is a domain-native simulated object rather than only curves, tables, cards, or abstract line art. Pass requires executed UI evidence for the stated mechanism; component presence, source-code intent, or a single easy happy path is insufficient. Actor reference: verify the action/evidence checklist through visible UI operations; do not finish success from component presence, source intent, or an unrelated easier interaction.
validation_scenarios.fairness_risk: Use a small finite component set. Do not let actor/evaluator substitute an easier example after a public or UI-advertised boundary case fails; count stale linked views, dummy controls, and impossible success states as real failures. If actor tooling cannot operate a visible drag/slider directly, try an actor-supported visible alternative on the same control; if the primary mechanism remains unreachable, record that as evidence instead of substituting a different feature.

evidence_requirements.expect: explains sinusoids and frequency components
changing a component changes both waveform and frequency bar

The UI must include a signal-lab simulation with signal generator, filter module, oscilloscope-style time trace, spectrum analyzer bars, and connected signal path; a waveform/curve alone is not sufficient.

evidence_requirements.surface: visible controls / primary visual / derived readouts
evidence_requirements.expect: At least two independent surfaces change consistently from the same canonical state; a static diagram plus unrelated readout is insufficient.
evidence_requirements.action: Use the most central state-changing control for this turn. First record the visible baseline value on the control plus at least two dependent surfaces, then change the control through a visible UI action. If a range click does not change the value, try direct text input on that same range/text control before giving up. Do not use source code alone as evidence.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Quote the exact before and after control value plus two dependent visible outputs such as readout value, plotted marker, warning text, selected item, table row, or diagram label. If only the control label changes while dependent surfaces do not, report partial or failure.

evidence_requirements.expect: The UI must either update according to the domain rule or explicitly explain why the state is impossible; stale values, impossible success states, or generic success text count as failure.
evidence_requirements.action: Exercise one high/low, valid/invalid, legal/blocked, narrow/wide, or correct/wrong contrast that is directly implied by the public request. Prefer a contrast with a predicted qualitative outcome, not a cosmetic setting.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Record the attempted contrast, the expected domain outcome, and the observed UI outcome. Do not replace a failed public or UI-advertised contrast with an easier passing example when deciding success.

evidence_requirements.expect: All linked surfaces must agree on the same selected entity/time/range/threshold; a view that still shows stale out-of-range data is failure.
evidence_requirements.action: Use the primary selection, filter, threshold, brush, or range control and inspect every linked surface named by the public request. If direct dragging fails, try visible numeric range inputs, preset buttons, keyboard focus plus arrow keys, or direct input on the same control when available; if no visible path works, report the primary interaction as unreachable rather than substituting an unrelated card click.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Record the selected value/range and at least three linked surfaces when present. Name any surface that remains out of sync, unchanged, or unreachable.

turns.prompt: Explain the idea of Fourier components, then build an interactive UI with a time-domain waveform and matching frequency bars for a few sinusoidal components. Please make it feel like a signal lab with generator/filter/oscilloscope modules, not only standalone curves.
Add low-pass and high-pass filters with a cutoff slider. Show the mask in frequency space and the reconstructed waveform after filtering.
Add a noise component and a before/after denoise comparison so I can see which frequency the filter removes.
Add sampling-rate control and show aliasing when the sampling rate is too low for one of the components.
Make a filter-design practice mode where I choose settings to preserve the target tone but remove noise, then get frequency-based feedback.
